column1: dangerous|Able to cause harm or injury.|The warning sign marked a dangerous path.
dare|To be brave enough to try something.|Do you dare to try the tallest slide?
day|The time between one midnight and the next.|We spent the day making pictures together.
dear|Loved or valued very much.|My dear friend made me a birthday card.
deceive|To make someone believe something that is not true.|The story's fox tried to deceive the other animals.
decency|Kind and fair behaviour.|We should treat everyone with kindness and decency.
decent|Good enough, or kind and fair.|We found a decent spot for our picnic.
decision|A choice you make after thinking.|Choosing the blue kite was an easy decision.
delicious|Tasting very good.|The fresh strawberries were delicious.
dependable|Able to be trusted to do what is needed.|My dependable friend remembered to bring the paints.
descent|A journey or movement downwards.|Our descent down the hill was slow and careful.
desert|A very dry area with little rain.|The camel walked across the sandy desert.
dessert|A sweet food eaten after the main meal.|We had fruit and yoghurt for dessert.
device|An object made to do a particular job.|A torch is a useful device in the dark.
devise|To think of a plan or way to do something.|We will devise a game for the whole class.
didn't|A short way of saying did not.|I didn't forget my reading book today.
dinosaur|An animal that lived millions of years ago.|We saw a huge dinosaur model at the museum.
disagree|To have a different opinion.|We can disagree and still be good friends.
disappoint|To make someone feel sad because something was hoped for.|Rain might disappoint the children waiting for sports day.
discipline|Practising sensible behaviour or working carefully towards a goal.|Learning an instrument takes patience and discipline.
discussion|Talking together about a subject.|Our class had a discussion about caring for wildlife.
disobey|To do something against a rule or instruction.|The puppy would sometimes disobey the command to sit.
dissent|To disagree, or a difference of opinion.|One pupil voiced dissent about the new game rule.
division|Sharing or splitting something into equal parts or groups.|We used division to share the counters equally.
do|To carry out an action or activity.|I will do my drawing after lunch.
dodge|To move quickly out of the way.|I had to dodge the rolling football.
dogs|More than one animal often kept as a pet.|The dogs played together in the park.
dolphin|A clever sea animal that breathes air.|A dolphin leapt above the sparkling water.
donkey|An animal like a small horse with long ears.|The donkey waited beside the farm gate.
door|A moving panel used to enter or leave a place.|Please close the door gently behind you.
double|Twice as much, or made of two parts.|Eight is double four.
doubt|Feeling unsure about something.|I had no doubt that my friend would help.
dough|A thick mixture used to make bread or pastry.|We shaped the soft dough into bread rolls.
down|Towards a lower place.|The ball rolled down the grassy hill.
draft|An early version of a piece of writing.|I wrote a draft before making my best copy.
dramatically|In a way that is striking or full of feeling.|The actor waved dramatically as the curtain opened.
draught|A current of air that comes into a room.|A cool draught came through the open window.
draw|To make a picture with lines or marks.|I like to draw animals with coloured pencils.
dream|A story or pictures in your mind while sleeping.|I had a dream about flying over the sea.
drew|Made a picture with lines or marks.|She drew a rainbow above the little house.
dried|Became dry or made something dry.|My coat dried in the warm sunshine.
dropped|Let something fall.|I dropped my pencil beside the desk.
dropping|Letting something fall.|The tree was dropping leaves onto the path.
dry|Not wet.|I put on dry socks after our rainy walk.
each|Every one, thought about separately.|Each child chose a different colour.
echo|A sound heard again after bouncing off a surface.|My shout made an echo in the tunnel.
edge|The outside line or border of something.|Draw a neat border around the edge of the page.
effect|A change caused by something.|Sunshine had a good effect on our seedlings.
egypt|A country in north-east Africa.|We learnt about ancient pyramids in Egypt.
eight|The number after seven.|The spider has eight legs.
eighth|Coming after the seventh in order.|My book was eighth in the pile.
electrician|Someone who installs or repairs electrical equipment.|The electrician repaired the lights in our classroom.
elephant|A large animal with a trunk and big ears.|The elephant used its trunk to drink water.
enclosure|An area that is fenced or surrounded.|The rabbits hopped around their grassy enclosure.
energy|The ability or strength to do things.|A good breakfast gives me energy for the day.
enjoyable|Pleasant and fun to do.|Our trip to the park was enjoyable.
enjoyment|The feeling of liking something you are doing.|We read the funny story with enjoyment.
equip|To provide what is needed for an activity.|We will equip the art room with new brushes.
equipped|Provided with what is needed.|The classroom was equipped with books and pencils.
essential|Very important and needed.|Water is essential for our garden plants.
even|Flat and smooth, or divisible into two equal whole groups.|Six is an even number.
exaggerate|To describe something as bigger or greater than it really is.|Do not exaggerate how tall your sandcastle is.
except|Not including something.|Everyone chose blue except me.
existence|The fact of being real or alive.|The museum showed evidence of dinosaurs' existence.
expansion|Something becoming larger or spreading out.|The school's expansion added two new classrooms.
expectant|Waiting excitedly for something to happen.|The expectant children watched the stage curtain.
expectation|A belief about what might happen.|We waited in expectation of a funny surprise.
experience|Something you have done, or knowledge gained by doing things.|Our first camping trip was an exciting experience.
experiment|A careful test to find out what happens.|We did an experiment to see which seeds grew fastest.
expression|A look or words that show a feeling or idea.|Her happy expression showed that she liked the present.
extension|An extra part added to make something longer or larger.|We built an extension onto our model house.
extreme|Very great or far beyond what is usual.|The plants needed shade during the extreme heat.
fair|Treating people equally and kindly.|We made a fair plan so everyone had a turn.
familiar|Known to you because you have seen it before.|The song sounded familiar to our class.
famous|Known by many people.|The famous author signed our books.
fancy|Decorative or special in a way that looks impressive.|She wore a fancy hat in the school play.
fare|Money paid for a journey on public transport.|We paid the bus fare before finding our seats.
farmyard|The area around a farm's buildings.|The hens wandered around the farmyard.
farther|At or to a greater distance.|We walked farther along the beach to find shells.
fascinate|To interest someone very much.|The colourful insects fascinate our class.
fatter|Having more body fat or a wider shape.|The caterpillar grew fatter as it ate the leaves.
fattest|Having the most body fat or the widest shape.|We chose the fattest pumpkin for our display.
february|The second month of the year.|My birthday is in February.
fetch|To go and get something and bring it back.|Please fetch the blue box from the shelf.
few|A small number.|A few birds landed on the fence.
fiction|Stories about imagined people or events.|I enjoy reading fiction about friendly monsters.
fictitious|Made up rather than real.|The detective in our story is fictitious.
field|An open area of land.|The sheep were eating grass in the field.
finally|After everything else or after a wait.|We finally reached the top of the hill.
find|To discover where something is.|Can you find my pencil under the table?
first|Before all the others in order.|I was first to choose a library book.
five|The number after four.|I drew five stars on my picture.
flew|Moved through the air using wings or a machine.|A robin flew across the garden.
flies|Moves through the air, or small flying insects.|The kite flies high above the park.
floor|The surface you stand on inside a room.|We sat on the floor to hear the story.
fly|To move through the air.|We watched the butterflies fly over the flowers.
food|Things that people and animals eat.|We packed healthy food for our picnic.
foot|The body part at the end of your leg.|I balanced carefully on one foot.
football|A game where players kick a ball towards a goal.|We played football together after school.
for|A word showing a purpose or who something is meant for.|This thank-you card is for my teacher.
forcible|Done using force.|The story's giant made a forcible push on the gate.
foreign|From another country.|We enjoyed learning a greeting in a foreign language.
forty|The number equal to four tens.|There were forty beads in the jar.
forward|Towards the front or the direction you are facing.|Take one careful step forward.
forwards|Towards the front or the direction you are facing.|The little train moved forwards along the track.
fossil|The remains or mark of a living thing preserved in rock.|We found a fossil shaped like a shell.
fought|Tried hard against something or took part in a fight.|The gardener fought to save the plants from the storm.
frantically|In a hurried and worried way.|We searched frantically for the missing class hamster.
frequency|How often something happens.|We recorded the frequency of birds visiting the feeder.
frequent|Happening often.|The garden had frequent visits from a robin.
frequently|Often.|We frequently read stories together after lunch.
fresher|More new, cool or recently made.|The air felt fresher after the rain.
freshest|The most new or recently picked or made.|We chose the freshest apples from the basket.
frisky|Lively and playful.|The frisky lamb bounced across the grass.
fudge|A soft sweet made with sugar, milk and butter.|We shared a small piece of vanilla fudge.
full|Holding as much as it can.|The basket was full of ripe apples.
funny|Making you laugh.|The funny little monster made us giggle.
furniture|Large useful objects in a room, such as chairs and tables.|We moved the furniture to make space for our game.
gem|A precious stone.|The pretend crown had a shiny blue gem.
giant|An imaginary person much larger than ordinary people.|The friendly giant waved to the children.
giraffe|A tall African animal with a very long neck.|The giraffe reached leaves at the top of the tree.
girl's|Belonging to one girl.|The girl's red kite flew above the park.
girls'|Belonging to more than one girl.|The girls' bags were beside the classroom door.
give|To pass something to someone else.|I will give my friend a birthday card.
glamorous|Looking exciting and full of special style.|The actor wore a glamorous costume for the show.
gnat|A very small flying insect.|A tiny gnat flew near the pond.
gnaw|To bite something many times.|The rabbit likes to gnaw a wooden chew toy.
go|To move or travel somewhere.|We will go to the park after lunch.
goal|Something you aim to achieve.|My goal is to practise a little each day.
gold|A valuable yellow metal, or its colour.|I painted a gold star on the card.
good|Kind, useful or of a high standard.|It felt good to help my friend.
government|The people who make decisions about running a country.|The government makes decisions about public services.
grammar|The rules for putting words together correctly.|We checked the grammar in our sentences.
grander|Larger or more impressive.|The second sandcastle was grander than the first.
grandest|The largest or most impressive.|Our class built the grandest model castle.
grate|To rub food into small pieces on a rough tool.|An adult helped me grate cheese for lunch.
grew|Became bigger or developed.|Our sunflower grew taller than the fence.
groan|A low sound showing discomfort or disappointment.|The story's troll gave a groan when it rained.
grow|To become bigger or develop.|We watched the tiny seedlings grow.
grown|Became bigger or developed.|Our pumpkin has grown much bigger this week.
guarantee|A firm promise that something will happen or work.|The shop gave us a guarantee for the bicycle.
guard|To watch over and protect someone or something.|The castle dragon would guard the treasure chest.
guessed|Suggested an answer without being certain.|I guessed the number of shells in the jar.
guest|Someone invited to visit.|Our guest brought a story to read to us.
guide|To show someone the way or help them learn.|The ranger will guide us around the nature trail.
gym|A room or building used for exercise and sport.|We played a balancing game in the gym.
half|One of two equal parts.|We shared the apple so each person had half.
happily|In a happy way.|The children played happily in the garden.
happiness|The feeling of being happy.|The surprise visit filled us with happiness.
harass|To keep bothering or upsetting someone.|It is unkind to harass someone who wants quiet.
has|Owns something, or has done something.|My friend has a blue bicycle.
hasn't|A short way of saying has not.|She hasn't finished her drawing yet.
have|To own something or experience something.|I have a red pencil in my bag.
he|A word used for a boy or man already mentioned.|My brother smiled because he liked the story.
he'll|A short way of saying he will.|He'll bring the football to the park.
head|The body part with your brain, eyes, ears, nose and mouth.|I wore a warm hat on my head.
heal|To get well again after being hurt.|The small scratch began to heal.
hear|To notice a sound with your ears.|I can hear a blackbird singing nearby.
heard|Noticed a sound with your ears.|We heard music coming from the school hall.
heart|The body part that pumps blood around your body.|My heart beats faster when I run.
heel|The back part of your foot.|The sock had a small hole at the heel.
her|Belonging to a girl or woman, or referring to her.|My sister put her book on the shelf.
herd|A group of animals of the same kind.|A herd of cows grazed in the field.
hesitancy|A pause or uncertainty before doing something.|His hesitancy showed that he needed more time.
hesitant|Unsure and slow to act.|I felt hesitant before trying the new game.
hesitation|A pause because you feel unsure.|After a little hesitation, I joined the game.
hideous|Very ugly or unpleasant to look at.|The story's troll wore a hideous muddy hat.
high|Far above the ground or another level.|The kite flew high above the trees.
hiked|Went for a long walk, often in the countryside.|We hiked along the woodland path.
hiker|Someone who takes long walks in the countryside.|The hiker carried a map and a water bottle.
hiking|Taking a long walk in the countryside.|Our family enjoys hiking on gentle woodland trails.
hindrance|Something that makes doing a task more difficult.|The fallen branch was a hindrance on the path.
his|Belonging to a boy or man.|My brother put his coat on the peg.
history|Things that happened in the past.|We learnt about our town's history at the museum.
hold|To keep something in your hand or arms.|Please hold the paint pot while I open it.
hole|An empty space or opening in something.|A rabbit peeped out of a hole.
home|The place where someone lives.|We walked home together after school.
honk|A loud sound made by a horn or goose.|We heard a goose honk beside the pond.
hope|To want something to happen and think it might.|I hope the seeds grow into bright flowers.
hopeless|Without hope, or having little chance of working.|The broken paper boat seemed hopeless until we repaired it.
horrible|Very unpleasant.|The story's giant made a horrible muddy mess.
horribly|In a very unpleasant way.|My wet socks squelched horribly inside my boots.
horse|A large animal that people can ride.|The horse walked slowly beside the fence.
hospital|A place where people receive medical care.|We visited our cousin in hospital.
how|A word used to ask about the way something happens.|Can you show me how to fold the paper?
huge|Very big.|We built a huge sandcastle at the beach.
humbly|Without boasting or acting more important than others.|She humbly thanked everyone who had helped her.
hummed|Made a tune with your lips closed.|My friend hummed a tune while drawing.
humming|Making a tune with your lips closed.|I heard someone humming in the classroom.
humorous|Funny or amusing.|We read a humorous poem about a penguin.
hunted|Looked carefully for something.|We hunted for smooth stones beside the stream.
hunter|Someone or something that searches for something.|The treasure hunter followed the clues on the map.
hunting|Looking carefully for something.|We were hunting for shells on the beach.
hurt|To cause pain or feel pain.|My sore foot hurt after the long walk.
hutch|A small shelter for an animal such as a rabbit.|The rabbit rested in its cosy hutch.
